pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which strategy would you use to see what a newspaper article is about? (1 mark)
   A. Painting
   B. Scanning for a number
   C. Cutting
   D. Skimming

2. Which is a character in a story? (1 mark)
   A. The rainy season
   B. A girl called Neema
   C. A shady tree
   D. The end

3. What is a debate? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of poem
   B. A song
   C. A game of football
   D. A discussion in which two sides give opposite views with reasons

4. What does a conjunction do? (1 mark)
   A. Names a thing
   B. Shows a feeling
   C. Describes a colour
   D. Joins words or sentences

5. In writing, what is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. A poem
   C. Words telling someone what to do
   D. A story

6. Why should you ask permission before using someone's phone? (1 mark)
   A. It is illegal to touch phones
   B. It belongs to them and needs care
   C. Phones never break
   D. It is a game

7. Which adjective describes colour? (1 mark)
   A. tall
   B. silver
   C. large
   D. thin

8. What is a conman? (1 mark)
   A. A person who tricks people to get money
   B. A farmer
   C. A shopkeeper
   D. A teacher

9. Which interjection shows a request for silence? (1 mark)
   A. Hurray
   B. Shh
   C. Aha
   D. Bravo

10. Which comma use is correct? (1 mark)
   A. When the bell rang we, ran.
   B. When the bell, rang we ran.
   C. When the bell rang, we ran.
   D. When, the bell rang we ran.

11. What is a talent? (1 mark)
   A. A book
   B. A rule
   C. A skill you are good at
   D. A kind of food

12. Which question word asks about a person? (1 mark)
   A. Who
   B. When
   C. How many
   D. Where

13. What is the main idea of a passage? (1 mark)
   A. The last word
   B. The page number
   C. What it is mostly about
   D. The date

14. What should you check in a partner's story? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. Only the paper colour
   C. Only the pen
   D. Title, characters, setting, problem and ending

15. Plural means (1 mark)
   A. more than one
   B. nothing
   C. the biggest
   D. only one

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Name three parts of a simple form. (3 marks)

17. Give three uses of capital letters in English. (3 marks)

18. State three steps for reading your part in a dialogue. (3 marks)

19. Write one instruction from the road safety dialogue. (2 marks)

20. Explain two differences between an advert and a news item. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Skimming
   You want the main idea.

2. B — A girl called Neema
   Characters are the people or animals.

3. D — A discussion in which two sides give opposite views with reasons
   A debate is an organised argument of a motion.

4. D — Joins words or sentences
   Conjunctions are joining words.

5. C — Words telling someone what to do
   Instructions say what to do.

6. B — It belongs to them and needs care
   Respecting others' property is polite.

7. B — silver
   Silver is a colour.

8. A — A person who tricks people to get money
   A conman deceives others.

9. B — Shh
   Shh asks for quiet.

10. C — When the bell rang, we ran.
   A comma follows the when part at the start.

11. C — A skill you are good at
   A talent is a natural ability.

12. A — Who
   Who asks about people.

13. C — What it is mostly about
   The main idea is the central point.

14. D — Title, characters, setting, problem and ending
   Peer review checks the elements.

15. A — more than one
   Plural nouns name two or more.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, instructions, fields, signature, date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence, names of people and places, the word I, days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each use.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, underline your lines, practise them, watch the punctuation, wait for your cue.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look right, then left, then right again. (or Cross at a zebra crossing.)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a correct instruction and one for a complete sentence.

20. (4 marks)
   Answer: An advert aims to persuade people to buy, while news informs about events. An advert gives a price and where to buy, while news gives who, what, where and when.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for each difference.
